characteristics.cultivar: Samidori, Yabukita, Okumidori and shade-grown cultivars
characteristics.harvestSeason: First flush, after 3–4 weeks of shade cultivation
characteristics.steeps: Whisked with bamboo chasen, single-serving suspension

description.short: Stone-ground powdered green tea ground from shade-grown tencha leaves — the spiritual centerpiece of the Japanese tea ceremony
description.overview: Unlike other teas, matcha is not steeped and discarded; the whole leaf is micro-milled and suspended in water, making every sip an intimate communion of beverage and ritual practice.
description.liquor: Opaque, dense vibrant green with a velvety micro-foam froth
description.aroma: Fresh, sweet grassy, marine nori nuances
description.taste: Intense savory umami sweetness, subtle pleasant bitterness, thick creamy texture
description.processing: Shading bushes 3–4 weeks before plucking (boosts L-theanine and chlorophyll, cuts bitterness) → harvest → steam fixation without rolling → drying flat (tencha) → slow granite stone milling into micron-fine powder

history.origin: Powdered, whisked green tea originated during Song Dynasty China (10th–13th centuries), where the practice virtually disappeared after the Mongol conquest.
history.development: Zen monks brought the practice to Japan, where it evolved into the philosophical and spiritual discipline of Chanoyu (the Japanese Tea Ceremony), steeped in Zen aesthetics and wabi-sabi.
history.modern: Uji remains the historic benchmark for top ceremonial grade matcha, while the tea has expanded globally into culinary staples, lattes, and confections.
interestingFacts: While powdered tea vanished in China by the late Ming Dynasty, Japan preserved it and elevated it to a high philosophical art form.
Traditional granite stone mills turn at agonizingly slow speeds, producing merely 30 to 40 grams of ceremonial matcha per hour to prevent friction heat from scorching the fragile leaf.
